correctness.rationale: Direct reciprocals give z_n(t)=f^n(z0)+(s/R^n)R^t f^t(z0)(f^t(z0)+1) exactly. Expanding f^t around its fixed point proves a strictly convex real-t exponential sum (and quadratic for R=1). Its endpoint difference yields the unique threshold xcrit=(R-1)/(1+R^(n/2)) for R>1, with negative squared branch excluded by z0>0; for 0<R<=1 a strictly positive one-step difference forces the last endpoint. The proof covers all real positive parameters and integer n>=2 including ties. Independent exact-rational code checks 1332 finite parameter cases and 7992 terminal placements, which are not substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The literature-led result is distinguished by its exact scalar product-form mating map, one treated generation, global endpoint placement, sharp initial-condition switch and dose-independent threshold. Exact comparisons with the inspected original models show no direct statement or trivial implication. Semantic research records and source searches returned no covering claim. This is a best-knowledge originality decision, with substantive inaccessible fuller literature identified and no claim of exhaustive priority proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical motivated pest suppression problem, all n possible one-dose intervention dates are classified by a closed-form endpoint rule and a sharp pest-density switch independent of sterile dose. An associated exact target-attainment dose follows. This replaces finite-horizon pulse-timing search with a transparent biologically interpretable boundary, and is not a mere tabulated special case or a reformulation of standard untreated Beverton–Holt equilibria.
